candidates.title: Starter Pack Syntax
candidates.pitch: The visitor is dealt a subject card for a thing rather than a person (a rainy Monday, a rink snack bar at the second intermission, a first week with a new roguelike) and fills a cobblestone-style mosaic of six tiles from a tray of hand-drawn vector items. A live grammar linter labels every tile with its job (the unmistakable anchor, the niche specific, the filler, the ironic turn) and scores the pack on balance, recognisability and sting. A reverse mode shows a finished pack and asks which subject it was; any pack exports as a PNG and as a shareable link.
candidates.whyNow: The starter pack is a Reddit-born format that has stayed active for years, so the grammar is timeless; the page also takes a seasonal subject deck keyed to the run date. I could not verify a single format that dominates this particular week (trend lists disagree), so the hook is the structure, not a news item.

research.summary: The starter pack is a well-documented, Reddit-centred collage format: a plain title plus a handful of images that together stand for a stereotype or situation. Wikipedia and Know Your Meme both trace it to a late September 2014 Twitter post, and the community later split off derivative templates where one image is swapped. Linguists have started treating memes as having rules of composition (labelled-object templates, multimodal grammar), which supports a page that makes the slots and roles explicit. Every subject in the page is a thing or situation, never a group of people or a private person, and all art is drawn in code. Trend lists for early October 2026 come from marketing blogs and do not agree on one dominant format, so no news claim is made.

facts.claim: The starter pack meme is traced by Wikipedia and Know Your Meme to a Twitter post dated 27 September 2014.
Researchers and a student project describe memes as structured artifacts with composition rules and labelled-slot templates, so slot roles can be named explicitly.
As of 2026-10-10, per Know Your Meme, the Loyal But Dangerous spinoff began on the starter pack subreddit in May 2021 and later versions often replace one image (single source, shown as reported).
As of 2026-10-10, trend lists from marketing blogs disagree on which meme format dominates early October 2026 (single commercial source, not presented as fact).

design.coreLoop: Draw a subject card, fill six tiles from a twelve-item tray, read the linter's verdict on each tile's role, swap items to fix balance and sting, then lock the pack. Repetition stays interesting because each subject has its own hand-authored item matrix (typicality plus role tags), the linter explains why a swap helps, and reverse mode flips the skill from composing to decoding.
sophisticationHooks: Grammar linter: every item carries per-subject typicality 0 to 3 and a role tag (anchor, specific, filler, turn); rules flag two competing anchors, no turn, or all filler, and name the fix
Reverse mode: a finished pack is shown and the visitor picks the subject from four; distractor subjects are chosen to overlap on filler items so the specifics decide
Cobblestone mosaic layout: one large anchor tile and five irregular tiles packed with a mortar gap, rendered in SVG and exported to PNG through canvas
Daily subject seeded from the run date, 18 subjects, shareable URL hash holding subject plus six item ids, so a friend can open your exact pack
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: 18 subject cards, about 70 drawn SVG items (simple geometric glyphs), the per-subject matrix, linter rules and scoring, build mode, reverse mode, PNG export, hash state, light and dark, reduced motion, keyboard placement (arrow plus enter), about/making-of panel listing only verified sources. Cut: free-text item entry, user-uploaded images, any real photo, multiplayer.
risks: Hand-authoring 18 by 70 typicality values is the main time sink; mitigate with tag-derived defaults and hand-tuning only the top three items per subject
Stereotype drift: subjects are restricted to things and situations, never groups or named people, and the about panel states the rule
The origin facts rest on Wikipedia and Know Your Meme, which may share lineage; the page presents them as 'per Wikipedia and Know Your Meme' and makes no claim about this week's trends
Scoring can feel arbitrary; the linter must show its reasons, and the score is labelled as a game score, not a verdict on humour

candidates.title: Format Drift
candidates.pitch: The visitor writes one tiny joke into an original drawn template (a two-panel contrast, an escalating four-tier ladder, a three-figure triangle or a plan-goes-wrong strip) and releases it into a simulated gossip chain. Each retelling mutates the joke in a small, named way (a role swap, an extra rung, an ironic flip, a literalised word, a topic substitution), growing a layered tree of variants whose edit distance from the original is shown on every branch. The visitor then acts as the audience and chooses which variants survive to be retold, steering the lineage until the final descendant is barely recognisable beside the original.
candidates.whyNow: Timeless rather than news-bound: published studies reconstruct descent trees of meme variants, and the expanding-brain ladder and three-figure labelling formats are still reused constantly. Evolution as a toy is novel for the studio and gives a screenshot-worthy side-by-side of ancestor and descendant.

research.summary: Researchers have repeatedly modelled memes as things that mutate when copied. A study of thousands of Facebook meme variants builds ancestor-to-descendant trees and reports that edit distance grows along copy chains, while two other arXiv papers build trees of image-macro variants and a dendrogram of frog-meme clusters. The expanding-brain format started in a Reddit joke called Whomst and is a four-image escalation; the three-figure labelling format has role slots that people relabel for any topic. Those documented structures become the mutation operators. The simulation is invented and labelled as such; it does not claim to reproduce any measurement.

sources.title: Information Evolution in Social Networks
sources.snippet: Facebook study tracking thousands of meme variants; builds variant trees, reports that variants further apart in a chain differ more in edit distance, and cautions that the genetic analogy is open.
sources.note: Mutation along copy chains with edit distance.

sources.title: MemeSequencer: Sparse Matching for Embedding Image Macros
sources.snippet: Builds a tree from pairwise distances between image macros of one template, linking children by shared imagery or shared text.
sources.note: Independent paper that arranges meme variants as a descent tree.

sources.title: Towards Understanding the Information Ecosystem Through the Lens of Multiple Web Communities
sources.snippet: Builds a dendrogram of frog-meme clusters (525 clusters across 23 memes) using a custom distance metric.

sources.title: Galaxy Brain (Know Your Meme)
sources.snippet: Says the escalating-brain series grew out of the Whomst joke, with an early popular version on a Reddit meme forum on 31 January 2017, and is often used ironically to imply the opposite ranking.
sources.note: Origin of the escalation ladder; the irony remark and the January 2017 date rest on this page alone and are shown only as reported.

sources.title: Dictionary.com's Top 10 Memes To Know How To Use
sources.snippet: Says the original had four images, from a small brain beside 'who' up to a glowing head beside 'whomst'd'.
sources.note: Independent confirmation of the Whomst origin and four-step shape.

sources.title: distracted boyfriend meme (Daily Dot)
sources.snippet: Reads the three figures as 'you', the thing you should focus on, and the passing distraction.
sources.note: Role slots of the three-figure format.

sources.title: Distracted boyfriend meet stars meme summer (Hollywood Reporter)
sources.snippet: Notes that the tempting figure was relabelled with everything from natural events to drinks to ideologies.
sources.note: Independent confirmation that the slots are relabelled freely.

facts.claim: Published studies arrange meme variants as descent trees or dendrograms built from pairwise distances (Facebook meme study, MemeSequencer, frog-meme clustering).
The Facebook meme study reports that variants further apart in a copy chain differ more in edit distance, and notes the biological analogy is only partly established.
The expanding-brain ladder began as an escalating four-image series from the Whomst joke, as covered by both Know Your Meme and Dictionary.com.
As of 2026-10-10, per Know Your Meme, the escalating-brain format is often used ironically to imply the opposite of its literal ranking (single source, shown as reported).
The three-figure labelling format has role slots (the person, the current focus, the tempting alternative) that are relabelled for arbitrary topics.

design.coreLoop: Write a seed joke into a template, release it for three retellings, read each new variant with its mutation named, pick survivors, and repeat for up to eight generations. Operators interact (an irony flip after an extra rung reads differently from before), the tree shows divergence at a glance, and players learn which mutation each template is most vulnerable to.
sophisticationHooks: Five or six named mutation operators acting on structured slots: role swap, add rung, drop rung, irony flip, literalise, topic substitute via a hand-made neighbour graph of about 150 concepts
Selection pressure: the visitor's pick decides survivors; an auto-select 'algorithmic feed' mode favours the most extreme variants and visibly collapses diversity, to show what selection does
Layered tree view as a canopy of nodes, each a mini rendered panel, with edit distance on each edge and a final ancestor-versus-descendant side-by-side card
Original art only: four stick-figure and glyph templates drawn in SVG, with URL-hash state holding template, seed words and the chosen path so lineages are shareable
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: four templates, the operator engine with seeded random so hashes replay exactly, the concept neighbour graph and ladder dataset (about 25 ladders of four rungs), tree and side-by-side views, feed-mode toggle, keyboard navigation, light and dark, reduced motion, about panel listing only verified sources and labelling the simulation as invented. Cut: free-form text mutation, image upload, real templates or photos, any claim of measured accuracy.
risks: Quality of mutated text depends on the hand-made graph and ladders; the engine should degrade to structure-only mutations when typed words are unknown
Mutations may yield flat jokes; mitigate by curating operator outputs with templates tested on the 25 ladders before the build freeze
The page must say clearly that the simulation is invented and not a replication of the cited studies
Know Your Meme irony claim is single-source and is shown only as 'per Know Your Meme' if at all
The three-figure template is described by original drawings, never the stock photo or any real person
